signals.entity: Viva.com / VivaBank Single-Member Banking Company S.A.
signals.signal: [regional] The Treasury of the Republic of Cyprus awarded its state electronic-payments contract to VivaBank Single-Member Banking Company S.A. (successor to Viva Payments Services S.A.), the Viva.com banking entity. Value EUR 3,920,000 for the first part plus EUR 172,942 for the second part; total duration 67 months (1 month technical preparation, 4-6 months system integration, 36 months core services, plus two successive optional 12-month extensions). Scope: operating the Cyprus government Payment Gateway (PGW) behind Gov.cy, Smart Checkout online processing, card and account-to-account (A2A) payments, AND the procurement, installation and maintenance of ALL physical card-acceptance POS terminals across Cyprus public services, using Viva's 'Tap on Any Device' softPOS (a phone/tablet app that turns an ordinary NFC device into a card terminal, no dedicated hardware). Annual managed payment volume expected to exceed EUR 1.5bn, covering direct taxes, vehicle-licence renewals and social-insurance contributions. The award was finalised 15/07/2026 and the contract signed with VivaBank on 12/08/2026; technical implementation runs through 2027. The tender began 07/01/2022 and was delayed roughly four years by bidder appeals. Roster note: Viva.com is tracked in competitors.json for GR, RO, SK and SI only - Cyprus is a NEW country for it.
signals.implies: This is a direct hit on Printec's POS-terminal and terminal-management line (Verifone/Castles plus TMS) in Cyprus: the single largest addressable terminal estate in the country - every public-service counter - has just been locked to a competitor for at least five and a half years, and it is being served with a software terminal rather than hardware Printec could supply. It also plants Viva.com, which Printec already meets in Greece, Romania, Slovakia and Slovenia, inside Cyprus with a state reference. Printec's realistic move is not the state estate but the commercial banks and the terminal-servicing layer: Viva must still physically deploy and maintain terminals at public offices island-wide, which is exactly the managed field-service work Printec sells.
signals.likelihood: Contract signed and running; POS rollout and technical implementation land during 2027
signals.followup: Approach Viva.com Cyprus about subcontracted terminal deployment, installation and field maintenance for the public-service POS estate, and separately re-qualify Bank of Cyprus, Hellenic Bank, Alpha Bank Cyprus, Eurobank Cyprus and AstroBank for terminal management before Viva's Tap-on-Any-Device reference is used against Printec commercially.

signals.signal: [local-peer] JCC Payment Systems Ltd - the bank-owned Cypriot card processor and dominant acquirer, and the incumbent operator of the Cyprus state electronic-payments service since 2010 - LOST that contract to Viva.com. JCC lodged a final appeal on 08/04/2026 with ten grounds of annulment; the appeal was dismissed on 15/07/2026 with all grounds rejected as unfounded and unsupported, which released the award. JCC's litigation is what stretched a tender opened 07/01/2022 across four years. This is a materially CHANGED position for a vendor already on the roster: JCC remains the Cyprus card-processing incumbent and the state's citizen electronic-identity supplier, but it has now been beaten on its home ground by a foreign PSP on a state contract.
signals.implies: Printec has read Cyprus as a market where JCC is simultaneously the biggest competitor and the only viable channel partner. That reading needs updating: JCC has just been shown to be beatable, and it is losing volume it has held since 2010. That makes JCC more likely to want technology partners to defend its remaining estate - which is the opening for Printec's terminal management (TMS), softPOS and transaction-monitoring (INETCO) lines - and it simultaneously proves to Cypriot buyers that a non-Cypriot supplier can win. Both readings favour Printec engaging JCC now rather than treating it as immovable.
signals.likelihood: JCC defensive technology investment plausible within 6-12 months as it absorbs the volume loss
signals.followup: Open a partner conversation with JCC Payment Systems on terminal management, softPOS and transaction monitoring, explicitly framed around defending its commercial acquiring estate now that the state volume is gone. Obtain the full appeal decision to identify what technical grounds JCC argued - it reveals what the Treasury actually scored on.

signals.entity: Veridos GmbH (Giesecke+Devrient / Bundesdruckerei joint venture, Oranienstrasse 91, Berlin)
signals.signal: [global] Veridos GmbH won the Cyprus Migration Department / Ministry of Interior contract for an end-to-end eMRTD issuance solution (eMRTD = electronic machine-readable travel document, i.e. biometric passports and ID cards), national reference 1/2023/TAPM/KD. Scope per the notice: enrolment system, personalisation system, PKI system, SPOC system and related services. Payable amount EUR 22,900,450 against an estimated EUR 34,550,000 - Veridos won at about 66% of the buyer's estimate. Restricted procedure, award criterion lowest price, 4 tenders received, no subcontracting declared. Contract issue date 18/12/2024; award recorded 28/07/2026 and the TED contract-award notice 525822-2026 published 29/07/2026, roughly 19 months after conclusion. Veridos is not in competitors.json, and neither is its parent Giesecke+Devrient, which this cycle also took the Banka Slovenije BPS M7 sorter maintenance to 2032 (EUR 1,890,000), the Bulgarian National Bank BPS C5/C7 modules (EUR 181,000) and, via G+D ePayments GmbH, the Czech state printer's dual eIDAS chip modules (EUR 216,000).
signals.source_name: TED (EU Official Journal) - contract award notice 525822-2026
signals.implies: Sovereign credential issuance in Cyprus is closed to Printec for the life of this contract, so Printec's digital-identity line (Namirial onboarding, eIDAS/EUDI e-signature) should not chase the state. The realistic Cyprus openings are downstream and bank-side: every Cypriot bank - Bank of Cyprus, Hellenic Bank, Alpha Bank Cyprus, Eurobank Cyprus, AstroBank - must re-tool its eKYC and document-verification to read the new Veridos-issued eMRTD/eID credential, and enrolment kiosks sitting in FRONT of the Veridos back end are Printec self-service territory. More broadly, this fixes the Giesecke+Devrient group as an active competitor inside the footprint on three fronts at once - identity in Cyprus, banknote sorting in Slovenia and Bulgaria, and card chip supply in Czechia.
signals.likelihood: Contract signed 18/12/2024 and running; bank-side eKYC re-tooling demand 6-18 months
signals.followup: Add Veridos GmbH and the wider Giesecke+Devrient group to competitors.json. Pull the underlying restricted-procedure contract notice for 1/2023/TAPM/KD to name the other three shortlisted bidders - that is the Cyprus identity competitive set. Then pitch Namirial/eIDAS onboarding and enrolment kiosks to the five Cypriot banks that must verify the new credential, not to the state.

signals.signal: [global] [STANDING - dated 13/01/2026] NCR Atleos announced a strategic agreement with Epirus Bank to modernise and expand its Greek ATM network using the Atleos ATM-as-a-Service (ATMaaS) model - i.e. Atleos owns and runs the machines and the bank pays per transaction/per machine - drawing on the Cashzone network (stated as 20,000 ATMs across Europe and 300,000 worldwide). Atleos provides the full network lifecycle: location selection, installation, maintenance and operational support. Deployment began November 2025 and was to complete in phases over roughly three months. The machines carry DUAL BRANDING - Epirus Bank and Cashzone - and offer cash withdrawal and balance enquiry. No ATM count and no contract value were disclosed; do not infer either. The announcement names no distributor or channel partner.
signals.implies: This is a channel risk, not a competitor win, and it is the most important structural item on the Greek beat: Printec's largest partner is selling ATM outcomes DIRECT to a Greek bank as a service, with its own retail brand on the fascia, in a model that removes the hardware sale and the field-service contract Printec would otherwise hold. Epirus Bank is precisely the profile - a small expanding bank without the scale to run its own estate - that Printec should be winning with NCR hardware plus x-core and telemetry. If ATMaaS becomes the default for small Greek banks and cooperatives, Printec's Greek ATM channel economics change fundamentally. Printec's counter is to own the ATMaaS delivery layer regionally rather than cede it: field services, monitoring, cash optimisation (APTRA OptiCash) and multivendor software are all things Atleos must source locally.
signals.likelihood: Structural; expect further Greek ATMaaS conversions among cooperative and small banks over 6-18 months
signals.followup: Escalate to Printec's NCR Atleos partner management: establish whether Printec can be the local delivery arm for Cashzone/ATMaaS in Greece and the wider footprint rather than being bypassed. Separately, pre-empt the ATMaaS pitch at the Greek cooperative banks (Epirus, Chania, Thessaly, Karditsa, Pancretan/CrediaBank) with a Printec managed-ATM commercial model. Re-check whether the Brink's acquisition of Atleos changes Cashzone's European strategy.

signals.entity: Central Bank of Cyprus (licensing regime for payment and e-money institutions)
signals.signal: [regulator] The Central Bank of Cyprus overhauled its licensing process for Payment Institutions and Electronic Money Institutions with effect from Monday 03/08/2026. Changes: a new mandatory PRE-APPLICATION EXPLORATORY STAGE before a formal application, carrying a non-refundable EUR 5,000 fee; the formal application fee doubled from EUR 5,000 to EUR 10,000; CBC power to require enhanced due-diligence reports from qualified firms at either the exploratory or the assessment stage; and automatic treatment of persistently unresponsive applications as withdrawn. Separately, the new Internal Organisation and Governance of Electronic Money Institutions Directive of 2026 came into force on 29/05/2026. The CBC states the aims are transparency for applicants and earlier identification of good-repute issues.
signals.implies: This changes the shape of Printec's Cyprus competitive set rather than any single vendor. Raising the cost and scrutiny of a Cyprus PI/EMI licence slows the arrival of new small acquirers and softPOS entrants - the class of competitor that has been eroding terminal economics - and pushes value toward the already-licensed incumbents (JCC, payabl., Pale Blue, Viva.com). The new governance directive also generates immediate compliance, AML and internal-controls remediation demand at every existing Cypriot EMI, which is addressable by Printec's AML/KYC and transaction-monitoring lines and is the same demand Complytek is chasing.
signals.likelihood: In force now; EMI governance remediation demand over the next 6-12 months
signals.followup: Verify the change on the primary source - centralbank.cy licensing-and-supervision pages for payment institutions and electronic money institutions - with a desktop browser User-Agent. Then build a target list of currently licensed Cypriot EMIs/PIs from the CBC register and pitch AML/transaction-monitoring remediation against the 29/05/2026 governance directive.

signals.signal: [local-peer] [STANDING - dated 26/03/2026] payabl. launched 'Tap to pay', a softPOS product (software that turns an NFC-enabled phone into a card terminal, with no separate hardware) for micro and SME merchants. It is live on ANDROID with iOS support stated as coming later in 2026 - that iOS step is the forward trigger. The app supports PIN entry, e-receipts and the full transaction set (sale, refund, reversal, tip) at no additional hardware cost, and integrates with payabl.one, the company's unified online-and-in-person payments platform, for a single view of transactions, payouts and settlement. payabl. is already on the roster as a Cyprus local-peer, but its move from card-not-present acquiring into IN-PERSON acceptance is a materially changed position.
signals.implies: A second Cypriot PSP has now crossed from e-commerce into physical acceptance without shipping a terminal, which directly compresses the addressable market for Printec's Verifone and Castles hardware plus TMS in the Cyprus SME segment - the same erosion Pale Blue's 'Paid' app started in May 2026 and Viva.com's Tap on Any Device now brings to the state estate. Three softPOS providers in one small market means Printec cannot defend Cyprus SME acceptance on hardware; the defensible ground is terminal management, certification, key injection, monitoring and field service for the merchants and banks that still need physical devices, plus attended and unattended use cases softPOS cannot serve.
signals.likelihood: iOS release stated for later in 2026 - a concrete forward step within the horizon

signals.signal: [local-peer] Peanuds, a Cypriot company building modular software for CARD- AND ACCOUNT-BASED financial products - letting fintechs launch card and account programmes through one platform - was one of seven companies selected for the Visa Innovation Program Europe 2026 edition covering Greece, Cyprus and Malta, announced 11/05/2026. The other six are AgriNow (Greece), Better (Israel), Cloudigo (Malta), Paytic (Canada), GYST (United States) and Outfindo (Czech Republic); Peanuds is the only Cypriot selection and the only one in card/account issuing. No funding figure, customer name or contract was disclosed and none should be inferred. Not in competitors.json.
signals.implies: Small and early, but it sits on Printec's card-issuing and payments-platform line in a market where Printec has no issuing incumbency and JCC holds the rails. A Visa-backed local card-programme platform is the kind of supplier a Cypriot EMI or challenger picks instead of an integrated vendor stack, and it is worth tracking now while it is cheap to engage rather than after it has bank references. Flagged under the rule that threat is independent of size.
signals.likelihood: Visa programme cohort runs through H2 2026; first named customer plausible within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Add Peanuds to competitors.json as a Cyprus local-peer in card/account issuing platforms and watch for its first named bank or EMI customer. Also review the remaining Visa Innovation Program Europe 2026 cohort each year - it is a cheap, reliable early-warning feed for new Greek and Cypriot payments entrants.

coverage_notes: Fresh full run (no checkpoint existed, so no resume). Coverage was built primary-source-first and deliberately away from the global names that have their own units. Routes actually used: (1) the Agent 2 tenders file of 27/08/2026 read directly for named Greek and Cypriot award winners, then each one re-opened on its own primary source (TED XML notices, Diavgeia decision records); (2) the Diavgeia openData API (search.json plus per-ADA decision JSON) queried in Greek on subject terms for banknote counters, ATMs and self-service - high noise, and the only genuinely useful yield was the ELTA cash-automation cluster, which is worth recording so the next run does not repeat the sweep at the same cost; (3) WordPress REST APIs polled directly where sites block normal fetching - banks.com.gr/wp-json (300 posts scanned), natechbanking.com/wp-json (57 posts), complytek.ai/wp-json (30 posts) - which is how the Natech AML push, the Complytek/VALEGA partnership and the Qualco acquisition run were all found rather than searched for; (4) Greek- and English-language press search across capital.gr, businessdaily.gr, cyprus-mail.com, cbn.com.cy and stockwatch.com.cy; (5) the Greece slice of source_catalogue_A6.json skimmed - the Natech wp-json route came from it and worked exactly as documented. Genuine gaps, stated honestly: no independent-ATM-deployer or CIT long tail was established for either country - Brink's Hellas and Brink's Cyprus dominate and Brink's has its own unit, G4S Cash Solutions Greece shows only recruitment activity as of June 2026 with no contract evidence, and no Greek or Cypriot independent ATM deployer surfaced at all, which is a real coverage hole rather than a nil; no Greek or Cypriot app-store softPOS sweep was performed (Google Play blocks automated fetches per the catalogue, and this would need a browser session or the google-play-scraper library), so newly launched softPOS apps in both markets remain unswept; the Cyprus Treasury cash-in-transit tender (~EUR 600,000 estimate) and the Electricity Authority of Cyprus banknote-counter tender (~EUR 55,000 estimate) flagged by Agent 2 were not resolved to winners, and those two would be the fastest route to the Cyprus cash-handling long tail next run; and Regtify (Nicosia) was identified as a Cypriot RegTech but is NOT reported as a signal because no trigger inside the recency window could be confirmed. Financials were not re-keyed from the scripted cache; the only vendor financials quoted are Qualco's own FY2025 disclosure as reported in Greek press (EUR 216m revenue, EUR 43m adjusted EBITDA), and no per-country ATM or POS unit count is estimated anywhere. Two signals carry an explicit [STANDING] prefix (NCR Atleos/Epirus Bank 13/01/2026 and payabl. Tap to Pay 26/03/2026) because their triggers predate the ~31/05/2026 freshness line; both are included for the forward step they imply, not presented as news. All confidence values are capped at Medium per the playbook.
access_issues: BLOCKED AND WORKED AROUND: eurokerdos.cyprustimes.com returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool on the payabl. Tap to Pay article - substituted the primary-market Cyprus Mail report of the same launch (cyprus-mail.com/2026/03/26/...), so the claim is sourced, not dropped. stockwatch.com.cy returned HTTP 403 on the Visa Innovation Program article - substituted the Cyprus Mail version of 11/05/2026. cbn.com.cy is a Next.js app with no WordPress API (wp-json returns the JS error shell); its articles were reachable only individually through the fetch tool, not enumerable, so cbn.com.cy could not be swept systematically. cyprus-mail.com/wp-json is behind a Sentry/bot wall and returns HTML rather than JSON, so Cyprus Mail also could not be enumerated - both Cypriot outlets had to be worked through search rather than crawled, which is a real ceiling on Cyprus discovery and should be escalated to a browser session next run. banks.com.gr/feed/ returned RSS that parsed to zero items, but banks.com.gr/wp-json/wp/v2/posts worked with a desktop Chrome User-Agent and returned 300 posts - use the wp-json route, not the feed. payabl.com/newsroom/ returned HTTP 404 (the newsroom has moved or been renamed); payabl. news was taken from Cyprus press instead. www.xtheodosis.gr 301-redirects cross-host to xtheodosis.com, so the older .gr deep links in search results do not resolve directly. The Diavgeia openData search.json endpoint silently IGNORES a 'q' parameter and returns an unfiltered date-ranged result set - the working parameter is 'subject', and issueDate comes back as epoch milliseconds, not a string; both are worth recording for future runs. NOT ATTEMPTED THIS RUN, still open: Google Play (blocks automated fetches, needs google-play-scraper or a browser session); centralbank.cy licensing pages were not re-fetched with a desktop User-Agent to confirm the 03/08/2026 licensing change on the primary source, so that signal rests on Cyprus Mail plus corroborating law-firm commentary rather than on the CBC itself.
